# (PART) Bio-Optical Modeling & Stability {-}

# Hierarchical Bio-Optical Models (`models.R`) {#models}

```{r ch6-setup, include = FALSE}
source('R/00_setup.R')
dir.create(file.path(PATH$figs, 'tables'), showWarnings = FALSE)
```

## Additive Beer–Lambert Model Formulation

We test ten candidate linear models that estimate specific light-attenuation coefficients ($\alpha_{\text{NAP}}, \alpha_{\text{DOC}}, \alpha_{\text{Chl }a}$) via ordinary least squares (OLS) with a fixed pure-water attenuation offset $k_w = `r round(get_k_w(), 5)`\text{ m}^{-1}$ and **no intercept**:

$$k_d - k_w = \alpha_{\text{NAP},g}\,\text{NAP} + \alpha_{\text{DOC},g}\,\text{DOC} + \alpha_{\text{Chl }a,g}\,\text{Chl }a, \qquad z_{SD} = \frac{1}{k_w + \alpha_{\text{NAP},g}\,\text{NAP} + \alpha_{\text{DOC},g}\,\text{DOC} + \alpha_{\text{Chl }a,g}\,\text{Chl }a}$$

Here $g$ indexes the stratification group: continental USA (Model 1), water-body type alone (Model 2), EPA Ecoregion Levels I–IV without water-type separation (Models 3, 5, 7, 9), or EPA Ecoregion Levels I–IV crossed with water-body type (Models 4, 6, 8, 10). Every modeled group requires $> `r P$zone_min`$ training matchups.

```{r fit, include = FALSE}
models <- get_models()
perf   <- model_performance(models, get_training())
write_csv(perf, file.path(PATH$figs, 'tables/table1_aquamatch.csv'))
s1     <- table_s1(models)
write_csv(s1, file.path(PATH$figs, 'tables/tableS1_coefficients_aquamatch.csv'))
```

```{r models-fig, echo = FALSE, fig.width = 10, fig.height = 4.3, fig.cap = '(a) Explained variance (R²) across Models 1–10, comparing ecoregion-only models (circles) against ecoregion × water-type models (triangles). (b) Distribution of fitted specific attenuation coefficients across the 39 strictly positive Level III ecoregions in Model 7 compared with the continental global fit (Model 1, vertical dashed lines).'}
p_r2 <- perf %>%
  mutate(
    level_f = factor(level, c('USA', 'Level 1', 'Level 2', 'Level 3', 'Level 4')),
    type_lbl = ifelse(by_type, 'By Water Type (M2, M4, M6, M8, M10)', 'All Water Types Pooled (M1, M3, M5, M7, M9)')
  ) %>%
  ggplot(aes(level_f, r2, group = type_lbl, colour = type_lbl, shape = type_lbl)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.9) +
  geom_point(size = 3.2) +
  geom_text(aes(label = paste0('M', model)), vjust = -0.9, size = 3.2, fontface = 'bold', show.legend = FALSE) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c('#1d6996', '#d95f0e'), name = NULL) +
  scale_shape_manual(values = c(16, 17), name = NULL) +
  scale_y_continuous(limits = c(0.42, 0.60), breaks = seq(0.45, 0.60, by = 0.05)) +
  theme_bw(base_size = 11) +
  theme(legend.position = 'bottom', legend.direction = 'vertical', panel.grid.minor = element_blank()) +
  labs(x = 'Spatial Ecoregion Hierarchy', y = expression(Explained~Variance~(R^2)),
       title = '(a) Model Predictive Skill Across Spatial Scales')

m1_coefs <- s1 %>% filter(model == 1) %>%
  transmute(`DOC (m²/g)` = DOC, `NAP (m²/g)` = NAP, `10 × Chl a (m²/mg)` = 10 * Chl_a) %>%
  pivot_longer(everything(), names_to = 'term', values_to = 'm1_val')

p_slopes <- s1 %>%
  filter(model == 7, NAP > 0, DOC > 0, Chl_a > 0) %>%
  transmute(`DOC (m²/g)` = DOC, `NAP (m²/g)` = NAP, `10 × Chl a (m²/mg)` = 10 * Chl_a) %>%
  pivot_longer(everything(), names_to = 'term', values_to = 'val') %>%
  ggplot(aes(val, fill = term)) +
  geom_histogram(bins = 18, colour = 'white', alpha = 0.85, show.legend = FALSE) +
  geom_vline(data = m1_coefs, aes(xintercept = m1_val), linetype = 'dashed', linewidth = 0.8, colour = 'black') +
  facet_wrap(~term, scales = 'free', ncol = 1) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c('#22c55e', '#d97706', '#38bdf8')) +
  theme_bw(base_size = 10) +
  theme(panel.grid.minor = element_blank()) +
  labs(x = 'Specific Attenuation Coefficient (dashed = Global Model 1)', y = 'Ecoregions',
       title = '(b) Model 7 Regional Coefficients (39 Positive Level III Ecoregions)')

p_r2 + p_slopes + patchwork::plot_layout(widths = c(1.25, 1))
```

## Table 1: Performance of Candidate Bio-Optical Models (Models 1–10) {#table1}

Every model's explained variance ($R^2$), root-mean-square error ($\text{RMSE}_{k_d}$), and common-sample Bayesian Information Criterion ($\text{BIC}$) are evaluated across all **`r fmt_n(nrow(get_training()))`** training matchups:

```{r table1-aquamatch, echo = FALSE}
perf %>%
  transmute(
    Level = level,
    Model = model,
    `By Type?` = ifelse(by_type, 'Yes', 'No'),
    `Groups (G)` = n_groups,
    `Group Size Median (Min – Max)` = ifelse(n_groups == 1, fmt_n(group_median),
      sprintf('%s (%s – %s)', fmt_n(group_median), fmt_n(group_min), fmt_n(group_max))),
    `R²` = round(r2, 2),
    `R² (exact)` = round(r2, 3),
    `RMSE kd (m⁻¹)` = round(rmse_kd, 2),
    `Fitted Coefs` = n_coef,
    `Strictly Positive Groups` = sprintf('%d / %d', n_groups - n_neg_groups, n_groups),
    `ΔBIC vs. Model 1` = fmt_n(round(bic_common - bic_common[1]))
  ) %>%
  kable(caption = paste0('Table 1: Summary of the 10 hierarchical general linear models evaluated across all ', fmt_n(nrow(get_training())), ' training observations.')) %>%
  kable_styling(bootstrap_options = c('condensed', 'striped'), full_width = TRUE)
```

::: {.decision}
**Why We Select Model 7 (`Level III Ecoregions`) for Continental Ternary Analysis**

```{r decision-numbers, include = FALSE}
pf <- model_performance(models, get_training())
m7c <- tidy_coefs(models) %>% filter(model == 7) %>% group_by(code) %>% summarize(pos = all(estimate > 0), n = first(n_group), sig = all(p_value < 0.001))
r2 <- function(i) sprintf('%.2f', pf$r2[i])
```

1. **Regional skill and parsimony:** Moving from the global model (Model 1, $R^2 = `r r2(1)`$) to Level III ecoregions (Model 7, `r pf$n_groups[7]` groups, $R^2 = `r r2(7)`$) increases $R^2$ by `r sprintf('%.2f', pf$r2[7] - pf$r2[1])` and lowers BIC by `r fmt_n(round(pf$bic_common[1] - pf$bic_common[7]))`, while keeping a median group size of $n = `r fmt_n(pf$group_median[7])`$ (`r fmt_n(pf$group_min[7])`–`r fmt_n(pf$group_max[7])`).
2. **Physical positivity:** In Model 7, **`r sum(m7c$pos)` of `r nrow(m7c)` Level III ecoregions** (`r sprintf('%.1f', 100 * sum(m7c$n[m7c$pos]) / sum(m7c$n))`% of observations) have positive slopes for all three constituents, with all three significant at $p < 0.001$ in `r sum(m7c$pos & m7c$sig)` of them. The remaining ecoregions use the global coefficients. Subdividing further to Level IV (Models 9–10) lowers the median group size to $n = `r fmt_n(pf$group_median[9])`\text{–}`r fmt_n(pf$group_median[10])`$, well below the $n \approx 1{,}000$ at which coefficients stabilize (`Figure S1`), for a gain in $R^2$ of `r sprintf('%.2f', pf$r2[9] - pf$r2[7])` to `r sprintf('%.2f', pf$r2[10] - pf$r2[7])`.
3. **River–estuary continuity:** Separating water types within Level III ecoregions (Model 8 against Model 7) adds `r sprintf('%.2f', pf$r2[8] - pf$r2[7])` to $R^2$ (`r r2(7)` to `r r2(8)`). Because Model 7 uses one set of regional slopes for streams, lakes, and estuaries, it can be applied along a river-to-estuary network without a step at the boundary between water types (`Figure 3`).
:::

## Comparison with Published Bio-Optical Benchmarks

```{r compare-numbers, include = FALSE}
c1 <- models$m1$coefs %>% select(term, estimate) %>% deframe()
tcm <- tidy_coefs(models); mall <- tcm %>% group_by(term) %>% summarize(x = mean(estimate)) %>% deframe()
```

In global Model 1 ($n = `r fmt_n(nrow(get_training()))`$), $\alpha_{\text{DOC}} = `r sprintf('%.4f', c1[['DOC']])`\text{ m}^2\text{ g}^{-1}$, $\alpha_{\text{NAP}} = `r sprintf('%.4f', c1[['NAP']])`\text{ m}^2\text{ g}^{-1}$, and $\alpha_{\text{Chl }a} = `r sprintf('%.4f', c1[['Chl_a']])`\text{ m}^2\ (\text{mg Chl }a)^{-1}$. Averaged over every group in Table S1, $\alpha_{\text{DOC}} \approx `r sprintf('%.1f', mall[['DOC']] / mall[['NAP']])`\,\alpha_{\text{NAP}} \approx `r sprintf('%.0f', mall[['DOC']] / mall[['Chl_a']])`\,\alpha_{\text{Chl }a}$.

**Putting our coefficients and published ones on one scale.** Published coefficients $k_i$ are per unit of diffuse attenuation $K_d$. Ours, $\alpha_i$, are per unit of $1/z_{SD}$. Because $K_d = a / z_{SD}$ (Section \@ref(screen-deep-dive)),

$$k_i = a\,\alpha_i \qquad\text{and so}\qquad a_{\text{implied}} = \frac{k_i}{\alpha_i}$$

For each constituent the table gives the published coefficient, our coefficient, and the conversion factor $a$ that would make them equal. Published measurements of $a = K_d \times z_{SD}$ have medians of 0.93 (turbid lakes), 1.86 (clear lakes) and 2.70 (stained lakes), with an overall range of 0.59 to 4.09 (Koenings and Edmundson 1991). If our coefficients agree with the published ones, the implied $a$ should fall in that range.

```{r bannister-table, echo = FALSE}
compare_bannister_literature(models) %>%
  kable(caption = 'Fitted coefficients (per unit of 1/z_SD) and published coefficients (per unit of K_d), with the conversion factor a = K_d x z_SD that each pair implies.') %>%
  kable_styling(bootstrap_options = c('condensed', 'striped'), full_width = TRUE)
```

```{r implied-a, include = FALSE}
ia <- as.numeric(compare_bannister_literature(models)[[4]])
```

Every pair implies a conversion factor between `r sprintf('%.1f', min(ia))` and `r sprintf('%.1f', max(ia))`, inside the published range of 0.59 to 4.09. For Chl *a* and non-algal particles the implied factor is 1.5 to 2.6, close to the published medians for clear and stained lakes. For DOC the implied factor sits near the two ends of the published range: high in lakes and low in estuaries. Theory predicts that direction, because coloured dissolved matter absorbs light without scattering it (large $a$). Most of the gap, however, comes from the nearly five-fold difference between the two published DOC coefficients, while our own lake and estuary coefficients differ by about 9%. DOC is therefore the constituent for which agreement with published values is weakest. Overall, our coefficients are consistent with the published ones once the difference between attenuation and Secchi depth is accounted for; they are not the same numbers, and should not be expected to be.

## Table S1: Fitted Coefficients, Standard Errors, and Significance {#tableS1}

All ten models' group sample sizes ($n$), specific attenuation coefficients, standard errors, and two-sided $t$-test $p$-values are exported to `figs/tables/tableS1_coefficients_aquamatch.csv`. Below are Models 1, 2, and the 39 strictly positive Level III ecoregion groups of Model 7:

```{r tableS1, echo = FALSE}
s1 %>%
  filter(model %in% c(1, 2) | (model == 7 & NAP > 0 & DOC > 0 & Chl_a > 0)) %>%
  select(model, code, type, n_group, NAP, DOC, Chl_a, p_NAP, p_DOC, p_Chl_a) %>%
  mutate(across(c(p_NAP, p_DOC, p_Chl_a), ~ format.pval(.x, digits = 2, eps = 1e-16)),
         n_group = fmt_n(n_group)) %>%
  kable(digits = 4, col.names = c('Model', 'Ecoregion', 'Water Type', 'n', 'α_NAP (m²/g)', 'α_DOC (m²/g)', 'α_Chl a (m²/mg)', 'p (NAP)', 'p (DOC)', 'p (Chl a)')) %>%
  kable_styling(full_width = FALSE, bootstrap_options = c('condensed', 'striped'), font_size = 11)
```

In the remaining 8 Level III ecoregions of Model 7, one unconstrained OLS slope estimate is slightly negative ($p \ge 0.10$) due to narrow local concentration ranges; during continental ternary projection (`Section 8`), those ecoregions automatically fall back to global Model 1 coefficients so all attenuation fractions remain strictly positive:

```{r m7-neg, echo = FALSE}
s1 %>%
  filter(model == 7, !(NAP > 0 & DOC > 0 & Chl_a > 0)) %>%
  select(code, n_group, NAP, p_NAP, DOC, p_DOC, Chl_a, p_Chl_a) %>%
  mutate(n_group = fmt_n(n_group)) %>%
  kable(digits = 4, col.names = c('Level III Ecoregion', 'n', 'α_NAP', 'p (NAP)', 'α_DOC', 'p (DOC)', 'α_Chl a', 'p (Chl a)'),
        caption = 'The 8 Level III ecoregions in Model 7 where an unconstrained slope estimate is non-positive (all p >= 0.10) and falls back to global Model 1 during ternary application.') %>%
  kable_styling(full_width = FALSE, bootstrap_options = 'condensed', font_size = 11)
```
